newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils close lower in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils close lower in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Most sectors of the European vegetable oil market closed lower on Tuesday in quiet pre-holiday trading.
The market will only be partially open on Wednesday owing to the Queen's Birthday holiday in the Netherlands.
Trade during the rest of the week is also expected to be affected by the May Day holiday in most of the rest of Europe and Malaysia on Thursday.
"A lot of people won't bother on Friday," said one trader.
Despite the steady undertone the market remains sensitive to movements on the futures markets in Asia and north America.
This resulted in a dip in soft oil prices towards the close following a lower opening in Chicago with an easier dollar adding to the downward pressure.
Soy oil closed 0.50 to 1.50 guilders lower after May traded at 105.00 and 104.75, Aug at 108.25, Aug/Oct at 108 and Nov/Jan at 106 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Rape oil finished one to 1.50 guilders lower after Aug/Oct traded at 106 guilders a 100 kilos.
Traders said although there were a number of trades reported the actual tonnage was low.
Coconut oil sellers were $5 to $10 down at the close while palmkernel oil was $2.50 to $7.50 down.
In a flurry of dealer trading coconut oil fetched $707.50 for Apr/May, $700 and $697.50 for May/Jun and $692.50 for Jun/Jul.
Palmkernel oil traded at $705 a tonne cif for May/Jun. The palm oil sector was quiet and close with sellers unchanged to $5 down in crude palm oil will products were $2.50 to $5 lower.
